content:
Selective Availability was a feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. Its removal happened in two distinct steps.

In May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the US government stopped using the feature to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

Then, in September 2007, the government announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability.

The first change ended its use. The second made its absence part of the next generation’s design—carrying the 2000 policy forward without treating the 2007 announcement as the moment the feature was switched off.
